title: Tansy and Peep Find the Moonbeam
markdown:
In a nursery with soft light lived Tansy the teddy bear and Peep the penguin chick.

Tansy was a soft bear. Fluffy gold fur. Gentle button eyes. Peep was a little penguin, round and white and full of wonder.

The nursery was cozy. Soft rugs. Warm blankets. And a special friend: a gentle moonbeam that loved to dance on the ceiling. It was not a loud moonbeam. It was a quiet moonbeam. It painted silver patterns. Tansy and Peep watched the patterns. Then they drifted off to sleep.

One evening they were snuggled. Their breathing was slow, like little sleepy waves. A tiny whisper of wind came through a tiny crack in the window. Not a wild wind. Just a little sigh. It was enough. It nudged the moonbeam.

Away the moonbeam floated. A silvery streak. Out of the window. Into the quiet night.

The nursery felt dim, like a favourite blanket had been pulled away. It felt a little lonely.

Tansy’s fluffy ears drooped. “Oh dear,” he whispered, soft as falling snow. “Our moonbeam is gone.”

Peep shuffled closer. His little white flipper rested on Tansy’s paw. “We must bring it back,” Peep chirped.

Tansy nodded. A little flutter of worry began in his fuzzy tummy. Leaving the cozy nursery felt like a very big thing. His paws wiggled, just a little. He wanted the moonbeam back. Without it, the room would stay dim. Sleep would be harder.

So, with the softest of sighs, Tansy and Peep tiptoed to the door. It creaked a little, like a sleepy old tree. Tansy held his breath. Button eyes wide. The hallway was long and peaceful and a little shadowy. The house was asleep. The furniture looked like big quiet shapes.

They shuffled along. Peep’s waddle made soft pat-pat sounds on the carpet. Tansy kept his eyes open. He looked for their friend. He listened.

A long curtain, like a soft grey river, swayed by a window. It rustled. Tansy gave a tiny squeak, like a lost button rolling. He held Peep’s flipper. He breathed. The house was still sleeping. The rustle was only the wind.

Then they saw it.

Through the big living-room window, on the wide wooden sill, lay their moonbeam. It looked a little pale. A little lost. All by itself in the cool night air.

“There it is!” whispered Peep.

The sill was just a little too high.

Tansy looked at the window. He looked at Peep. Peep’s eyes said, You can. Tansy took a deep gentle breath.

He stretched his little teddy arms. Reaching. Reaching. Reaching. Like a sprout reaching for the sun. His tummy felt wobbly. He leaned far. For a moment he thought he might tumble. His paws felt heavy. He remembered the moonbeam, alone and sad. He stretched a tiny bit more.

His fuzzy fingers brushed the cool silvery light. He cupped the moonbeam in his paws. It felt cool and soft, like moonlight made of silk.

They began the quiet journey back. The hallway did not seem so long now. The sleeping furniture looked like old quiet friends.

They tiptoed into the nursery. Tansy lifted his paws. The moonbeam floated up, up, up, a silent silver ribbon. It settled on the ceiling. It painted its familiar patterns.

The nursery was bright and cozy again.

Tansy looked at Peep. A warm soft feeling spread through him, like sunshine on fur. A shadow flickered on the wall. Tansy just smiled.

“Just a shadow,” he whispered.

They snuggled into their blankets. The moonbeam danced above. Sweet dreams. Safe and sound. Under the gentle familiar light.
